source_text: Ergo si audirent illi sacerdotes, quorum nunc dicta deluimus, dubitari utrum commixtio coniugalis bona esset, atque ab eis peterem corporane a Deo informata, faterentur. Hocque concesso, adderem utrum coniugia a Deo annuerent ordinata. Quo similiter confirmato, peterem denuo, utrum esset sine commixtione fetura. Hocque denegato, quid sequebatur? Videlicet, si nonnisi per Deum corpus, nonnisi per corpus commixtio, nonnisi per commixtionem fetus, ad eumdem auctorem pertinere et fetum et commixtionem, ad quem corpora pertinerent.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore if those priests, whose sayings we have now washed, heard it doubted whether marital mingling is good, and I asked of them whether bodies were formed by God, they would confess. And this having been granted, I would add whether they would grant marriages ordained by God. Which similarly confirmed, I would ask again whether there is offspring without mingling. And this having been denied, what followed? Namely, if a body is not except through God, mingling not except through a body, offspring not except through mingling, both offspring and mingling belong to the same author to whom bodies belonged.
pass_b_english: Suppose, then, that the bishops whose words I am now clearing heard it doubted whether marital union was good. I would ask them whether they acknowledged that bodies were formed by God. Once that was granted, I would add whether they agreed that marriage was ordained by God. With that likewise confirmed, I would ask again whether offspring could exist without union. Once this was denied, what would follow? Clearly, if a body exists only through God, union only through a body, and offspring only through union, then both offspring and union belong to the same author as bodies.

choices.why: Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
